what: Provenance for every ledger under bench/phase0-agent-native/ that stamps a measuredCommit. Those stamps name PRE-SQUASH BRANCH commits: this repository squash-merges, so the squash discards them and no third party can resolve them — three of five are contained by zero remote branches and survive only as unreferenced objects in individual clones. Every roadmap since 0.15 cites them as the provenance of its published numbers.
whyNotJustRepointTheStamps: Because measuredCommit is the experimental record, not a pointer. Repointing it would falsify what was measured, and effect-rows-benefit-ledger.json's stamp is additionally ARM_B_COMMIT — a frozen constant of a completed epoch, pinned by ppw-compile.py, ppw-analyze.py and PpWRowsRegistrationTests. Two of these ledgers are also byte-compared against their own generators, so a field added by hand would make them permanently 'stale'. The stamps stay; this file carries the resolvable equivalent beside them.

basisKinds.identical-src-tree: STRONGEST. A commit reachable from main whose `src/` tree is byte-identical to the measured commit's, verified with `git rev-parse <sha>:src` on both. Same compiler; a third party can check the numbers against it.
basisKinds.landing-commit-only: WEAKER, and said so. No commit reachable from main has an identical `src/` tree, so the exact compiler state was never landed as such. The commit named is the squash that carried the LEDGER onto main — where the numbers landed, not the compiler that produced them.
basisKinds.measured-on-top-of: The numbers were measured with the landing change APPLIED to the named commit, which is what regenerating a ledger inside the PR that moves it always means. The stamp its generator writes is HEAD at regeneration time, and the squash commit that will carry the change does not exist yet — the #1159 bootstrapping problem, and the reason this index exists rather than a rule that the stamp must equal the landing commit.

ledgers.note: #1191: regenerated at branch commit fbd52cd1357b86dff7bb5742b67991a33a145d4a with conditional-preservation changes applied to release/v0.19 ancestor 639fa93a. This is the reproducible release base, not an identical compiler tree. PropertyToken and StreetNumberComparer newly reach effects: enforced modules 324 -> 326, Calor0425 diagnostics 113 -> 117. Native call modifiers change MessageTemplateParser's first binding stop from Calor0208 to Calor0250 without changing its exclusion status. The historical #1176 measurement remains in git history.

#1188: both legs were regenerated at branch commit 487682479ef5a01fda4aadec06a00f1091762e35, with this PR's expression-match validation applied to release/v0.19 commit 743723cd. D-A lists one additional early rejection, the already-invalid conversion fixture 13-10.approved.calr; total demand remains 3123. The named release ancestor is the reproducible base, not a claim of an identical compiler tree.

Searched every commit reachable from main: none has an identical src/ tree, so this compiler state was never landed. The residual is real and is stated rather than hidden behind a stronger-looking stamp.

The measured commit is not present in this clone at all, so no tree comparison is possible. It is also ARM_B_COMMIT and must not move. Worth recording: it shares its first EIGHT hex characters with main's real v0.15.0 release commit 3bb2601e3ff83597ddf2f27dcc334b6399ab97ea, which is why short shas looked right to every reader until now.
